subject: history
title: Learning, printing & oceanic expansion
objective: A changing scale of knowledge and exchange

lesson.opening: How did changes in communication and trade alter the possibilities of political and cultural life?

sections.heading: The institutional thread
sections.body:
Humanism and patronage

Printing and the circulation of texts

Oceanic routes and commercial institutions

sections.heading: A model to test
sections.body: Connect technologies to patrons, markets, institutions, and existing routes. Keep inventions, diffusion, and applications separate in the chronology.

sections.heading: Keep the question
sections.body: How did changes in communication and trade alter the possibilities of political and cultural life?

activities.prompt: Which happened first: “European movable-type printing develops” or “Da Gama reaches India by sea”?
activities.hint: Compare the dates on the unit timeline.
choices: Da Gama reaches India by sea

activities.prompt: “The Cape route alone explains the growth of Portuguese power in the Indian Ocean.” — is that an event claim or an interpretation?
activities.hint: This assigns a decisive cause. Test the argument against existing trade, military force, local alliances, and commercial institutions.

activities.prompt: Put these events back in chronological order.
items: Da Gama reaches India by sea

activities.prompt: Explain how printing changes the conditions of argument without assuming that it determines what people believe.
activities.instructions: A few sentences are enough. Cite a passage when it helps.
